PICO-8 · Design Document

Zombie Pathfinding Algorithm

Dijkstra Map (Distance Field) + Greedy Descent

Overview

Idea: instead of computing a path per-zombie, I build one distance map from the player (P) outward across all walkable tiles. Every tile gets a cost = how many steps from P. Then each zombie just looks at its neighbors and moves to whichever one has the lowest cost — greedy descent.

This is basically a Dijkstra map (or flood fill / BFS distance field). Scales great — all N zombies share one map, and each zombie move is O(1).

Example Grid

5×5 map — P=(1,5), Z=(5,1). Walls at (4,1),(3,2),(4,2) form a pocket that traps the naive delta-reduction path.

1 6 5 4 █ Z
2 5 4 █ █ 6
3 4 3 4 5 6
4 3 2 3 4 5
5 P 1 2 3 4
Legend
P — Player (cost 0)
Z — Zombie start
█ — Wall (impassable)
Number — BFS cost from P

Z=(5,1). Delta to P = (−4,+4).
Naive: go left → (4,1)=wall.
Diagonal: (4,2)=wall. Trapped.

Actual path (cost 8 steps):
(5,1)→(5,2)→(5,3)→(4,3)
→(3,3)→(2,3)→(2,4)→(2,5)→P

Z has to go down first (away
from P) before it can route around.
Delta alone would never find this.

Phase 1 — Build Distance Map

01
Initialize

Set all walkable tiles to ∞. Walls get -1 (sentinel). Player tile = 0. Push player pos onto queue.

02
BFS flood fill

Dequeue a tile. Check each neighbor (4-dir or 8-dir) — if it's walkable and still at ∞, set its cost to current + 1 and enqueue it.

03
Repeat until queue empty

Every reachable tile ends up with its min distance from P. Anything still at ∞ is walled off / unreachable.

⚠ My original mistake: I was using delta = Z−P to only flood fill "toward player" directions. That breaks as soon as there's a wall in the way — the path might need to temporarily move away from P to get around it. Need to flood fill in all directions, no delta filtering.

Phase 2 — Zombie Movement (Greedy Descent)

01
Check neighbors

Each zombie looks at all valid neighbors (same dirs as flood fill). Skip walls and OOB tiles.

02
Move to lowest cost

Move to whichever neighbor has the smallest cost. If current tile is already 0, zombie reached P.

03
Tie-breaking (optional)

If 2+ neighbors tie for lowest cost, pick randomly — stops all zombies moving in perfect sync which looks weird.

Issues Identified in Original Notes

What I got wrong
Delta-restricted flood fill
Filtering by Z−P delta breaks pathing around walls. I noted this myself — "so this is wrong." BFS has to go all directions.
Single-pass update
One left-to-right sweep misses costs that need to propagate right-to-left. Need a proper queue, not a sweep.
Grid example inconsistency
My worked example assumed a clear diagonal path but the walls I drew might actually block it. Need to double-check these agree.
What I got right
Distance map concept
Build cost table from P outward, zombies descend it. Right idea, just the flood fill implementation was off.
Tie rule
"If reachable from 2+ directions, take smaller source + 1" — that's exactly correct BFS relaxation.
Greedy descent phase
Sharing one map across all zombies instead of running pathfinding per-zombie is the right move for PICO-8's perf budget.

Pseudocode

Build Phase
-- call once whenever player moves or map changes
function build_cost_map(px, py)
  -- initialize all tiles
  for y=0, map_h do
    for x=0, map_w do
      cost[x][y] = is_wall(x,y) and -1 or 32767
    end
  end

  cost[px][py] = 0
  local queue = {{px, py}}

  while #queue > 0 do
    local cx, cy = table.remove(queue, 1)  -- dequeue front
    for _, d in ipairs(dirs) do           -- dirs = 4 or 8 directions
      local nx, ny = cx+d[1], cy+d[2]
      if in_bounds(nx,ny)
      and cost[nx][ny] == 32767           -- unvisited walkable tile
      then
        cost[nx][ny] = cost[cx][cy] + 1
        add(queue, {nx, ny})
      end
    end
  end
end
Move Phase
-- call each update tick per zombie
function zombie_step(z)
  local best_cost = cost[z.x][z.y]
  local bx, by = z.x, z.y

  for _, d in ipairs(dirs) do
    local nx, ny = z.x+d[1], z.y+d[2]
    if in_bounds(nx,ny)
    and cost[nx][ny] >= 0               -- not a wall
    and cost[nx][ny] < best_cost
    then
      best_cost = cost[nx][ny]
      bx, by = nx, ny
    end
  end

  z.x, z.y = bx, by
end

PICO-8 Performance Notes

  • PICO-8 map is 128×128 max = 16,384 tiles. BFS over that is fine, but don't run it every frame — only rebuild when P moves to a new tile.
  • table.remove(queue, 1) is O(n) in Lua. For bigger maps I should look at a ring-buffer queue or just cap the search radius around P.
  • If exact pathing isn't needed, I can run a smaller sub-map centered on P to cut cost further.
  • All zombies share one cost map — no extra work per zombie, just the greedy descent step.
